chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa, the seller of Sabir, from Aban ibn Uthman from Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the child faces the midwife with his face, she becomes prohibited to him, and her children become prohibited to him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a midwife or her children after breastfeeding?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific condition for establishing milk kinship (rad') through the midwife, requiring the infant to face her directly during breastfeeding. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes a permanent marriage prohibition not only between the child and the midwife but also extends to her biological offspring, mirroring the status of full siblings. This ruling underscores the importance of physical proximity and direct nursing in forming the mahram relationship, a key concept in Islamic family law.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Abdullah Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad Bin Isa Baya’a Al Sabiry, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the child faces the midwife with his face, she would be Prohibited unto him, and her children would be Prohibited unto him (as well)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn ‘Isa Bayya’ al- Sabiriy from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If the child feels compassion toward al-Qabilah (special nurse who helps one’s mother during her giving birth and thereafter) she becomes unlawful to him for marriage as well as her children.’”
